claims.claim: Integral switching flows are exactly feasible points of an affine binary-parity lattice system.
claims.evidence: For source supply δ_o, integrality and 0≤x_0(v)−x_1(v)≤1 imply d_v:=x_0(v)−x_1(v)∈{0,1}. With q_v=x_0(v)+x_1(v), ε_v=q_v mod 2, and p_v=(q_v−ε_v)/2, necessarily ε_v=d_v, x_0(v)=p_v+ε_v, and x_1(v)=p_v. Substitution into conservation gives (2I−A^T)p=δ_o+((A^0)^T−I)ε, and the substitution reverses exactly. Because every nonterminal has a path to a sink, the uniform internal transition matrix is transient, so 2I−A^T is invertible. The adjugate congruence, nonnegativity test, and terminal-inflow formulas therefore characterize precisely the integral source switching flows.
claims.witness: Summing nonterminal conservation cancels all internal arcs and gives b_0+b_1=1. Thus each feasible integral point has terminal signature (1,0) or (0,1), exactly as required by the source switching-flow certificate theorem.
claims.search_method: Derived both directions algebraically from the source definition of switching flow, then independently proved transience using a uniform probability of reaching a sink within N steps.

claims.claim: At fixed positive-level width r, the affine system is block lower-Hessenberg and gives an exact reduction of ARRIVAL, but it retains N binary choices.
claims.evidence: If an edge goes from u∈L_j to v∈L_i, the definition of shortest-path distance gives j≤i+1. In A^T, the corresponding entry has row block i and column block j, so entries vanish whenever j>i+1; the same holds for (A^0)^T−I. These are block lower-Hessenberg matrices under the stated ordering. Claim 0 plus the source certificate theorem makes feasibility with b_1=1 equivalent to a YES instance. There remains one binary ε-coordinate for each of the N=rk nonterminals, and permitted long backward edges generate blocks arbitrarily far below the diagonal.
claims.witness: For any fixed ε, the nonsingular integer system has one rational p, whose integrality, sign, and terminal form can be checked in polynomial bit complexity. This establishes an exact reduction but not a polynomial search over all ε.
claims.search_method: Checked matrix indices directly against the source level definition and checked both directions of the reduction against the source switching-flow certificate theorem.

claims.claim: Width three admits at least 2^(N/3) distinct feasible parity vectors with the same terminal signature, even when every vertex is reachable from the origin.
claims.evidence: Every displayed edge stays in its indexed level or moves down exactly one level, and each vertex has a downward path of length i, so a_i,b_i,c_i have distance exactly i. From c_k one can descend the c-rail to c_i and then reach a_i and b_i. For each subset S, the unit c-rail flow has source supply one and terminal signature (0,1); adding the unit even-edge circulation a_i↔b_i independently for each i∈S preserves conservation and every terminal inflow. All positive outflows equal one, so the resulting ε-vector records exactly the chosen circulations and the always-active c-rail.
claims.witness: The 2^k subsets of {1,…,k} give 2^k distinct ε-vectors, while N=3k. The exact checker verifies levels, origin reachability, conservation, switch inequalities, terminal signatures, and parity-vector distinctness for k=1,…,7.
claims.search_method: Proved the construction parametrically and exhaustively checked representative depths with integer arithmetic.

claims.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
claims.evidence: For an absorbing terminal t, directed summation by parts gives x^−(t)−y^−(t)=Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v), since equal supplies cancel at every nonterminal and h_t is harmonic. Each d lies in [0,1], while |g_t(v)|=|h_t(s_1(v))−h_t(s_0(v))|/2≤1/2, hence each terminal coordinate has diameter at most N/2. Fixed total terminal inflow makes the first q−1 coordinates determine the last, so for fixed boundary size q there are at most (⌊N/2⌋+1)^(q−1) integral signatures. For φ≡1, the stated transient linear system realizes every prescribed d∈[0,1]^N, validating the sharpness assertion used later.
claims.witness: The checker constructs exact same-supply flows from prescribed imbalance vectors and verifies the dual identity and attained gap mass over the one-level and rail families.
claims.search_method: Re-derived the identity on directed arcs, proved the counting bound, and checked the imbalance-realization equation using exact rational elimination.

claims.claim: For fixed terminal count and fixed integral supply, all integral terminal-inflow signatures admitted by the fractional switching-flow polyhedron can be enumerated in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Each terminal-coordinate minimum and maximum is obtainable by rational linear programming. Claim 3 bounds the width of every resulting interval by N/2, so each contains only O(N) integers regardless of the magnitude of the fixed supply. Enumerating the first q−1 coordinates yields O(N^(q−1)) candidates for fixed q; the integral total supply determines the last coordinate. An equality-constrained feasibility LP accepts exactly those candidates realized by fractional switching flows. Thus the proposed enumeration is sound, complete, and polynomial in the input size for fixed q.
claims.witness: Every realizable integral signature lies in the optimized coordinate ranges and passes its own feasibility LP; conversely, each emitted vector comes with a feasible rational flow witness.
claims.search_method: Audited output size, endpoint bit complexity, total-inflow conservation, and both directions of the enumeration argument.

claims.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
claims.evidence: An edge can decrease shortest-path level by at most one. Because the finite uniform walk is absorbing almost surely, a walk beginning at level at least i hits L_{i−1} before absorption. The strong Markov property therefore places its hitting probability in [m_{i−1},M_{i−1}], proving nested ranges. Both successors of v∈L_i lie at level at least i−1, so |g(v)|≤W_{i−1}/2 and summation gives Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_iW_{i−1}. Claim 7 supplies a family where the left side is linear in the depth.
claims.witness: The exact checker verifies nested level widths and the displayed range inequality throughout the parametric rail family for multiple k and r.
claims.search_method: Proved the stopping-time argument directly from shortest-path levels and corroborated the inequality on exact rational examples.

claims.claim: At the one-positive-level boundary, the exact maximum gap mass is r/2; therefore the width-two stability constant fails at width three in the smallest possible depth.
claims.evidence: The universal pointwise bound |g(v)|≤1/2 gives total gap mass at most r/2. Giving every L_1 vertex even successor 0 and odd successor 1 yields h(v)=1/2 and |g(v)|=1/2, attaining the bound. With supply one at every vertex, flows (1/2,1/2) and (1,0) are feasible and their sink-1 inflows differ by r/2. Thus width three already has diameter 3/2, whereas the source width-two bound is one. One positive level is the least possible nonempty depth.
claims.witness: The exact checker verifies harmonic values, feasibility of both flows, the dual identity, and terminal difference r/2 for r=1,…,9.
claims.search_method: Established the universal upper bound and matched it with an explicit exact construction.

claims.claim: For every fixed r≥3, harmonic gap mass and same-supply fractional switching-flow diameter can be Θ(N), so the universal N/2 bound is asymptotically order-tight up to an r-dependent constant.
claims.evidence: Substitution into every harmonic equation confirms h(a_i)=i/[2(k+1)], h(b_i)=1−i/[2(k+1)], and h(c_i)=1/2. Summing the resulting gaps gives k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]. Each added centered vertex for r>3 retains value 1/2 and contributes the asserted gap, giving k[4+(r−2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)]. With N=rk and fixed r≥3 this is Θ(N). Claim 3 realizes the full gap mass as the terminal-inflow difference of two fractional switching flows with common supply φ≡1.
claims.witness: All vertices have their claimed level because every edge decreases the displayed index by at most one and each has a forward path. The checker solves the harmonic systems and constructs the extremal flows exactly for 2≤k≤8 and 3≤r≤7.
claims.search_method: Verified the harmonic formulas and sums symbolically, then checked graph levels, formulas, and extremal flow realization using rational Gaussian elimination.

claims.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three, and two positive levels already suffice for this failure.
claims.evidence: Both completions are simple binary graphs with L_1={a,b,c}, L_2={X,Y,Z}, and identical outgoing edges from L_1. Solving the harmonic equations gives completion A: (h(a),h(b))=(3/22,1/22), and completion B: (h(a),h(b))=(1/22,3/22). Thus the same preceding boundary order and identical current-level outgoing data admit opposite orders. With only one positive level there is no higher-level completion whose unseen edges can cause this phenomenon.
claims.witness: The exact checker independently derives both rational solutions, verifies all graph levels, and confirms that the L_1 local data agree exactly.
claims.search_method: Solved both six-vertex absorbing systems from scratch and checked the graph-model conditions.

claims.claim: These obstructions delimit the width-two proof strategy but do not settle fixed-width ARRIVAL.
claims.evidence: The constructions invalidate exhaustive parity enumeration, a width-independent harmonic diameter bound, and the width-two local-order mechanism. The LP result applies only after fixing the complete supply and permits fractional internal flows. None of these facts supplies a polynomial-time algorithm, a hardness reduction, or an exhaustive dichotomy for width three or any r>3. The draft explicitly preserves these limitations.
claims.witness: The exact affine reformulation still contains N binary coordinates, while the exponential circulation family shows that naïvely listing its feasible parity points can require exponential output.
claims.search_method: Compared the logical conclusions of claims 0–8 with the exact source target and checked that no unproved algorithmic inference was made.

target_evidence: The source asks for a determination of polynomial-time solvability for every fixed r>2, beginning with r=3. The draft supplies correct reformulations, fixed-supply subroutines, and counterexamples to several width-two proof mechanisms, but it expressly gives neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor a contrary complexity classification. Therefore it does not fully resolve the target, while the surviving results constitute material partial progress. Its claimed resolution of PARTIAL is accurate.
